Earlier today, it was reported that Milan had readied €70 million for the January mercato. With that money, the blueprint is to bring a upcoming young attacker and there are two choices: Nicolo Tresoldi and Endrick. However, the possibility of both joining cannot be ruled out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri.

According to recent reports, I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Another Nations League appearance delivered the inevitable for Viktor Gyokeres.

His brace in Sweden’s 3-2 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina made it eight consecutive Nations League games in which he has scored, a record he holds by himself.

Gyokeres has 12 goals in that run.

Whether Mikel Arteta spent his Saturday night tuned into the action from the Strawberry Arena is unclear, but we know exactly what his thoughts will have been.

Speaking after Gyokeres scored four goals in as many matches in the last international break, Arteta admitted: “Well, the first reaction is, ‘What am I doing that with me they don’t do this, or they haven’t been given the opportunity to do that?’.

According to recent reports, “That’s a natural one. But then you obviously are really happy.

“I’m very happy that they are able to help the national teams in that way, because I haven’t done it, but it should be one of the best feelings to represent your country and do it in such a way.”.

According to recent reports, arteta, then, will be having the same reflections again. How does he get more of the Gyokeres in a Sweden shirt for Arsenal?

In a recent development, win more penalties would be a good start. Both of Gyokeres’ goals against Bosnia came from the spot and he has now converted his last 29 penalties.

There is also the obvious caveat that the defences Gyokeres is coming up against at international level are not comparable to what he is facing for Arsenal.

According to recent reports, as well as his two goals against Bosnia, Gyokeres assisted Alexander Isak’s finish. He ran in behind the high line and squared brilliantly for the Liverpool striker, though the strike was ruled out for offside.

It was perfect decision-making and execution but it was also the kind of space that Arsenal are not afforded on a regular basis.

The Champions League clash with Slavia Prague earlier this month, particularly in the first half, was a rare example of Arsenal being allowed to play with that freedom and Gyokeres delivered probably his best performance in an Arsenal shirt.

However, for all there are obvious tactical differences, the difference in performance levels when Gyokeres is playing for club rather than country is still alarmingly stark.

Gyokeres has had four shots in each of his last three Sweden appearances. Incredibly, he has managed a total of just four shots across 11 matches for Arsenal in the Premier League and Champions League this season.

Industry observers note that it has often felt like a confidence glitch. Gyokeres looks right at home when leading the line for Sweden. He is the main man, taking free-kicks, penalties, and constantly his team-mates are looking to find him.

The difference in performance levels when Gyokeres is playing for club rather than country is still alarmingly stark.

Graham Potter has been important in that, emphasising at every opportunity just how crucial Gyokeres is to the team.

“He’s done brilliant for us when he’s been playing every week [for Arsenal], and he’s done brilliant for us when he hasn’t been playing every week,” Potter told The Independent ahead of this international break.

Industry observers note that gyokeres is not the main character at Arsenal. He knows Arteta will normally turn to Kai Havertz, especially in the big games, regardless of what form the German is in.

Havertz has struggled since picking up a hamstring matter in the last international break but he has still largely kept his place.

Even after Gyokeres played so well against Slavia and continued the big recent improvements in his hold-up play and combinations with those around him, he dropped back to the bench as Havertz started against Hull.

The striker debate is an ongoing one at Arsenal and on recent form, it feels as though the court of public opinion is edging back towards Gyokeres.

That is probably the biggest selection headache Arteta has ahead of Arsenal’s trip to face Newcastle on Saturday.

According to recent reports, as the Arsenal boss has admitted himself, he is not getting as much out of Gyokeres as Potter is. For a perfectionist like Arteta, that will be a major source of frustration.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 23:27.

Nicaragua and Montserrat will face off in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League play-in tie at the Nicaragua National Football Stadium in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time.

The Blue and White claimed a 2-1 victory away from home in the first leg and will head into the return fixture full of confidence as they look to finish the job in front of their home supporters.

Juan Cruz Real's side have endured a horror Nations League campaign, failing to pick up a single point from four matches.

They have scored only four goals and conceded 14 as they finished at the bottom of League A's Group A.

After four defeats in a row, Nicaragua produced a strong performance at Estadio Cibao, where they took full advantage of an extra man after the home side were reduced to 10 men inside the opening 20 minutes.

Despite going a goal down, an own goal from Samuel Fenton sparked a revival, while Efrain Mejia scored in the 72nd minute to give them a slender lead heading into the second leg.

Montserrat are the underdogs in this tie, having earned their place in the play-in round from League C, but they have shown few weaknesses so far.

Despite losing a man so early in the first leg, they still managed to find the net, meaning the tie remains very much in the balance heading into the return fixture.

Gabriel Calderon's side won all four of their matches in League C's Group A, scoring 11 goals and conceding just once.

Montserrat kept clean sheets in three of those outings, but they have never tasted victory against their opponents in four attempts, which could prove a psychological hurdle.

Nicaragua could look to field a similar side to the one that started the first leg, although Cruz Real may be tempted to hand right-winger Mejia a starting role after his impressive performance earlier this week.

Juan Barrera failed to make a significant impact in the previous match, but he is still likely to retain his place, with Jaime Moreno once again expected to make a cameo appearance from the bench.

The visitors will definitely be without Lenni Cirino, who was sent off in the first leg.

Captain Alex Dyer appeared to pick up an injury towards the closing stages of that encounter before being replaced by Vashim Roache, and his absence would represent a major blow.

Tyrone Baker may have to settle for a place on the bench, but versatile midfielder Kaleem Simon could come into the starting XI.

Nicaragua possible starting lineup:.

Mayorga; Gutierrez, Cano, Perez, Quijano; R Cole, Salinas, Hernandez, Mejia, Talavera; Smith.

Montserrat possible starting lineup:.

Carter-Rodgers; Cirino, Furlong, Dorsett, Townsend-West; Barzey, Kirnon, Dyer, Simon; Comley, Boatswain.

Sources indicate that nicaragua have failed to keep a clean sheet in their last six matches and have conceded the opening goal in five of those encounters. However, buoyed by their first-leg victory, we expect the hosts to produce a stronger performance on home soil and narrowly secure another win.

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono handed ban for tackle that led to Jesus de Miguel death

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (496 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games for his tackle that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.
  • The 25-year-old was sent off after his collision with De Miguel near the halfway line late in the Spanish second division match on November 2.
  • Recent findings suggest that de Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono’s knee had struck him in the chest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games for his tackle that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The 25-year-old was sent off after his collision with De Miguel near the halfway line late in the Spanish second division match on November 2.

Recent findings suggest that de Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono’s knee had struck him in the chest. The 30-year-old striker was taken to hospital where he died the following morning.

The Spanish Football Federation’s disciplinary committee has now issued the maximum suspension possible for Owono’s challenge.

A statement noted: ‘The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.’.

In his first statement since De Miguel’s death, Owono insisted he will ‘face whatever comes with the utmost respect’.

‘These are the most difficult days of my life. I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very hard to process what has happened,’ Owono said.

‘I feel immense pain at the loss of Jesus. I’m thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It has been revealed that ‘I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.’.

Speaking this week, FC Andorra manager Carles Manso noted that Owono is still considering his future in football.

‘He is deeply affected by the situation,’ Manso said.

‘We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.’.

Earlier this week, Spanish newspaper Marca reported that Owono is barely leaving his house following De Miguel’s death and is closely working with psychologists and doctors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Troy Deeney believes incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino should ‘make a statement’ by looking to sell Marcus Rashford.

Rashford failed to make an impact under Michael Carrick after returning to Old Trafford following his loan spell at Barcelona last season.

The 29-year-old missed the last five matches of Carrick’s tenure due to a hip injury, with Pochettino arriving as his replacement after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract with the Red Devils.

Reports earlier this week have suggested that Rashford could be a major winner of United’s latest appointment, with Pochettino very keen to work with the England international and get him back to his best.

But former Premier League striker Deeney believes Pochettino should not be so lenient with Rashford and must be willing to sell the forward in January if he doesn’t get back to his best promptly.

‘Poch must go in and take a huge sledgehammer to the toxic Carrington culture, accepting that things are not good enough,’ Deeney told The Sun.

‘Managers and those above need to stop fiddling around the edges and tackle the significant problem, otherwise there will be no progress.

Sources indicate that ‘United supporters might not like it, but Arsenal have shown the way and offered the blueprint. Rather than repeating what has failed, they must make a brave change. Someone substantial has to go, even if it means short-term pain.

‘Mesut Ozil, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Alexandre Lacazette were pushed out for the benefit of everyone. They were good players but carried a stink with them around the place.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Cut them out and everyone else can breathe, focus in training and start growing.’.

Deeney continued: ‘For the Red Devils, that has to be someone like skipper Bruno Fernandes or, once again, Marcus Rashford.

‘I can guarantee it now, Rashford will suddenly be fit for the Liverpool game. He will see a upcoming manager who likes energy and pace, he will think he can do all that.

‘He might even start well, get a few games, but then Pochettino will ask for more and he will not like it. Then all the bad traits will come back — he’ll be out and about and late for training all over again. The cycle begins and the damage returns.

‘Pochettino must make a statement, give these players until January to prove they are on board or get rid.’.

Latest transfer news and rumours.

Manchester United’s alternative targets to Mauricio Pochettino have been revealed.

The Red Devils were on the hunt for a new manager after sacking Michael Carrick last week, with the former midfielder relieved of his duties after just one win in 11 matches.

It left the Premier League side mired in the top-flight relegation zone, and searching for their eighth permanent head coach since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013.

Vinicius Junior has admitted that Arsenal’s push to sign him in the summer has impacted his form this season.

The Gunners held strong interest in him as they looked to kick on from their Premier League title win and make a marquee signing in attack.

Vinicius had entered the final 12 months of his contract at Real Madrid in the summer and there was strong speculation that he could leave the club.

With Real and Vinicius at a contract impasse and little progress made in negotiations, Arsenal made it clear they would meet the winger’s financial demands.

Mikel Arteta was desperate to sign the 26-year-old but the Brazilian ultimately ended up signing a latest six-contract at the Santiago Bernabeu.

They are, though, closing in on the appointment of former Tottenham and Brentford boss Thomas Frank on a two-and-a-half-year deal, with the Dane set to be in the dugout against Coventry.

It is now seven goals and nine assists in 20 appearances across all competitions for both club and country for Antonio Nusa so far this season, the latest of which has prompted Arsenal fans on social media to demand a January transfer.

Erling Haaland has said he is happy at Manchester City, after commenting on the club’s financial scandal.

During the autumn international break, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2018/19.

While City deny any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal, serious sanctions - such as points deductions, fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League - are likely if that fails.

According to reports, a hearing is to take place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

Should Man City relegated or be issued a huge points deduction, many have speculated that a number of the club’s stars will likely depart, including Haaland.

However, the Norway international - who is valued at £183million on transfermarkt and would have a host of clubs queuing up for his signature were he to leave the Etihad Stadium - has set the record straight on his future with a transfer update.

Scott continues to go from strength to strength for both club and country, earning his first senior caps for the Three Lions during the previous international break in recognition for his fine form in the Premier League.

The 23-year-old made his England debut off the bench in September’s 2-0 away win over the Czech Republic in the Nations League, with Rice having pulled out of the squad, before then being handed his maiden start by Thomas Tuchel in the 7-0 demolition of Croatia last month.

All four clubs, though, could be trumped by Real Madrid as they retain a buy-back clause.

Fulham defender Calvin Bassey has emerged as a shock target for new Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino.

That is according to the Telegraph, who claim the Nigeria international is expected to feature prominently on Pochettino’s list of targets for the January transfer window.

Bassey is approaching the final six months of his contract at Fulham, so could be available for a cut-price fee.

Belgium manager Rudi Garcia has revealed that he had two interviews at Manchester United about taking over as the club’s manager.

He told The Athletic: “I’d like to work in England and I met Darren Fletcher and John Murtough.

“It was an interim role and they asked me what I would do once it was over. I told them I would do so well that I would be staying in Manchester, but they gave the job to Ralf [Rangnick].”.

Toby Alderweireld has told Manchester United fans what they can expect to see from Mauricio Pochettino when he arrives as the club’s newly introduced manager.

The Belgian worked under Pochettino at Tottenham, forging one of the Premier League’s standout centre-back pairings with Jan Vertonghen under the Argentine’s stewardship.

Now, Pochettino, 54, will take the reins at Old Trafford, succeeding Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Wednesday after a run of 11 matches bearing just one win.

“You need to follow his blueprint,” Alderweireld explained to BBC Sport.

“If you don't follow his proposal, you're not coming back any more.

"If you're thinking about yourself, you're gone.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China’s one-child policy is probably the best-known population-control programme in history, yet in its first decade it barely changed the country’s fertility rate. Writing in Nature, Meng et al.1 show that the biggest drop in fertility after the policy’s introduction was driven by a change in how officials were incentivized to enforce it. This change accounts for about half of the fall in the country’s fertility rate during the 1990s.

Chelsea failed with an approach to sign Real Betis winger Jose Antonio Morante, according to reports in Spain.

The 19-year-old made his first-team breakthrough with Real Betis earlier this year and has made three appearances for the Spanish club this season.

In the summer, Morante was a key part of the Spain squad which won the UEFA European Under-19 Championship. He finished in the Team of the Tournament with five of his Spain teammates and ended the tournament as the joint-top scorer with four goals.

According to ABC Sevilla, Chelsea monitored Morante during the European Under-19 Championship and made an approach to the winger’s representatives in the summer transfer window.

However, Morante is understood to have personally turned down a move to Chelsea as he wants to become a first-team regular with his boyhood club Real Betis.

ABC Sevilla add that Chelsea have been ‘persistent’ with their interest but Morante has made it clear that he wants to stay with the Spanish club.

In July, Morante signed a latest deal with Real Betis which keeps him tied to the club until 2030 and includes a €30 million (£25m) release clause.

It has been revealed that "Being compared to Mourinho is too much, you're making me embarrassed! He's a legend and I have only just begun," Chivu noted.

"This is only my second year in the professional ranks. If I could achieve even a fraction of what he has won, I would be a very happy man, even happier than I am.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”.

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa noted. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”.

Industry observers note that some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

It has been revealed that konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Recent findings suggest that konsa, 29, has promptly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Sources indicate that thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

According to recent reports, the victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also notes plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his latest surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

In a recent development, “Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

Sources indicate that “I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”.

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

Sources indicate that they kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

Probably sums up Zubimendi’s season so far that he finally gets some meaningful minutes in the Premier League and ends up getting smashed in the face and covered in his own blood. This is after he got injured in a cool-down a few weeks ago. When your luck’s out...

Eight minutes added on at the Emirates.

Brilliant play from Oscar Bobb as he cuts inside on his left foot and bends a shot into the far bottom corner for the away side.

How have Arsenal reacted to their top scorer Saka being injured? Both of their centre backs have scored for the first time this season.

On his 200 Premier League appearance for Arsenal, Gabriel marks it with his first goal of the season.

It is a lovely move with slick one-touch passing. The ball is fed to White making a run down the outside and he clips the ball to the far post for Gabriel to head home.

OFF Merino, Lewis-Skelly, GyokeresON Calafiori, Guimaraes, Havertz.

Garner is booked for Everton now after barging into Merino off the ball.

Sources indicate that arteta is shown a yellow card for something. Not sure what for yet. But the Arsenal manager is looking to make some changes off the bench.

In a recent development, arsenal have been guilty of overplaying today. Opting for the extra pass rather than taking a shot. The game is open at the moment and that makes things dangerous for the home side.

Recent findings suggest that yellow card for Lewis-Skelly after bringing down Johnson. Gabriel is back on the pitch and seems happy enough to continue.

Arsenal have defensive options in Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori and Mosquera if Arteta wants to avoid taking any risks.

A worry for Arsenal as Gabriel jars his knee into the ground as he tries to clear the ball. The Brazilian is receiving treatment and hobbles off the pitch.

Industry observers note that gabriel immediately raised his hand for medical attention after making that clearance. He really extended his leg to get the ball away. Looks to be in a lot of pain.

It has been revealed that latest corner from Arsenal after Eze’s shot is blocked by Rohl. Rice’s delivery into the near post is headed clear to Odegaard, who shoots ambitiously from distance and Pickford collects the ball comfortably.

It has been revealed that arsenal get the match restarted. The longer the match goes on without extending the lead, Everton will think they have a chance.

Sources indicate that before today, Arsenal had averaged five corners per match in the Premier League this season. In the first 45 minutes here, they had 10 corners.

Yellow card for Mykolenko after he catches White wide on the right. Rice whips the ball in and Merino meets it with a flick goalwards but the ball goes over the bar.

That is the final touch of the half and the players are running off to get dry!

Raya is penalised for taking too long with the ball and Everton have a cheap corner. Danger is cleared by Arsenal as they force Everton back into their half.

In a recent development, the conditions are terrible at the moment. Heavy wind and rain causing havoc.

According to recent reports, A lot of set-pieces for Arsenal today as they continue to put Everton under the cosh. Can they take advantage of their dominance again before the break?

Arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

Another effort at goal for Madueke. This one is a snapshot from the edge of the box that goes into the side netting.

Courtesy of Opta: Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal in all competitions (not including penalties) since May of last season against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one.

Set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

Arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

A couple of early set pieces from Declan Rice. Everton do well to clear the danger. But have another one now...

Horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

On bouncing back from defeat...

Industry observers note that “Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”.

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

Recent findings suggest that “They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”.

In a recent development, “Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”.

Sources indicate that “A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

According to recent reports, this is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Sources indicate that today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”.

Recent findings suggest that this is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz.

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham.

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

In a recent development, arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

In a recent development, “I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes noted: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

Mauricio Pochettino has been tipped to complete the marquee signing of Como midfielder Nico Paz for Manchester United.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half year deal in Manchester and will join up with the squad ahead of their trip to Anfield to face Liverpool next Sunday.

United have made their worst start to a season in 40 years, and are right now without a league win since mid-August.

As he looks to arrest that slide, Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window as United look to fill gaping holes in their squad at left-back and forward areas.

But former Aston Villa forward Gabby Agbonlahor believes Pochettino may also look to move on senior players and earmarked Bruno Fernandes as one who might have an uncertain future under the Argentine.

Fernandes’ contract is up at the end of the season, with recent reports suggesting that the Red Devils captain has rejected a second contract offer from the club.

And speaking on talkSPORT, Agbonlahor mused: ‘Maybe Pochettino comes in and says, “You know what? I don’t like his attitude. I don’t like the way he throws his arms up at his teammates, the way he threw Michael Carrick under the bus. Can I go and get my own players?”‘.

Should Fernandes leave the club, Agbonlahor earmarked Como midfielder Paz as the perfect candidate to ‘refresh’ United’s squad.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Nico Paz – how good has he been?’ he added. ‘He’s the next star for Argentina.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Does Pochettino say, “You know what? I want him next summer from Como, make it happen”. Save the money on wages that maybe Bruno Fernandes wants.

‘So he might have his own ideas to get all these players out that maybe have been a little bit of a problem and to refresh the whole squad.’.

Paz tormented Michael Carrick’s side in the Champions League last month, scoring twice and providing an assist in a 4-1 victory, having grown into one of Serie A’s brightest talents under Cesc Fabregas.

The Argentine joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid, although Los Blancos do retain a £67million buy-back clause, which can be activated next summer.

Recent reports in Spain indicate that the possibility of a move to the Premier League appeals to Paz’s representatives, although Como’s transfer position and Real’s intentions will be a deciding factor.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Ojele | 15 Nov 2026 23:31, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 23:32.

Sierra Leone and Congo DR return to action in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers when they square off in the second of their Group E double-header at the Stade El Abdi on Tuesday.

While the Leopards will look to maintain their 100% record in the qualifiers and move another step closer to securing their place in next year’s continental showpiece, Sierra Leone head into the game under considerable pressure for a result, having lost their three matches so far.

Tasked with guiding Sierra Leone to a first Africa Cup of Nations tournament since 2022, French head coach Didier Gomes Da Rosa has failed to make his mark in the qualifiers, with the Lone Stars rooted to the bottom of Group E after the first half of the campaign.

While they revealed signs of promise, Sierra Leone blew a two-goal lead in the group opener on September 24, when they fell to a 3-2 loss against Zimbabwe in Morocco, four days before suffering a 1-0 loss at the hands of Equatorial Guinea at the Stade Omnisport Ahmadou Ahidjo.

Sierra Leone were left with a mountain to climb in the qualifiers on Thursday, when they were beaten 3-1 by DR Congo, with Yoane Wissa, Samuel Moutoussamy and Watford man Edo Kayembe hitting the back of the net to fire the Leopards to all three points.

Having missed out on the 2025 AFCON after an underwhelming qualifying campaign that saw them finish third in Group G with five points from six matches, Sierra Leone are one of just six sides yet to pick up any points in the qualifiers, leaving them with little margin for further errors and in need of significant improvement.

Meanwhile, Congo DR kicked off their AFCON qualifying journey on a high, claiming a 2-0 victory over Equatorial Guinea on September 24, four days before edging out Zimbabwe 2-1 at the National Sports Stadium thanks to strikes from Wissa and Moutoussamy.

However, a break from competitive action saw the Leopards fail to win their subsequent two outings, losing 2-0 against Uganda on October 2, three days before playing out a 1-1 stalemate with the Cranes in the second of their friendly double-header at the FNB Stadium.

Congo DR returned to action in the AFCON qualifiers with a comprehensive team display against Sierra Leone on Thursday to remain one of just four nations with a 100% record in the campaign and move one step closer to sealing a third appearance in the continental tournament since missing out in 2021.

Sebastien Desabre’s men, who are currently 40th in the latest FIFA World Rankings, sit top of the Group E standings with nine points from a possible nine, five points above Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea, who sit level on four points after the first three games.

Congo DR will be backing themselves to maintain their perfect record on Tuesday when they take on an opposing side who have lost each of their previous four meetings, conceding 11 goals and scoring just twice since September 2014.

Sierra Leone came out unscathed against DR Congo on Thursday, and we expect Da Rosa to name a similar XI at the Stade El Abdi, with Alie Conteh and Elfsborg striker Momoh Kamara spearheading the attack.

Amidst their struggles at the defensive end of the pitch, Da Rosa could opt for a change in the back four, with Alpha Turay, who made his debut in June 2023, coming into the mix to form the centre-back pairing with Kilmarnock man Michael John Kamara.

As for DR Congo, APS Atromitos Athinon midfielder Moutoussamy was forced off injured midway through Thursday’s clash, and the 30-year-old is a doubt for Tuesday’s matchup.

Should he fail to shake off the injury, Lorient man Noah Mbamba, who made his debut on Thursday, will push for his first start in the Leopards’ colours, teaming up with Edo Kayembe and Sunderland man Noah Sadiki at the centre of the park.

Up top, Wissa made it three goals in three AFCON qualifying games with his opener against Sierra Leone on Thursday, and the Newcastle United striker should lead the attack once again, forming the front three with Nathanael Mbuku and Almeria winger Brian Cipenga.

Sierra Leone possible starting lineup:.

In a recent development, sesay; Kakay, MJ Kamara, J. Turay, Tarawallie; Kanu, I.Turay, Kamara, Koroma; M. Kamara, Conteh.

Congo DR possible starting lineup:.

Epolo; Pedro, Mbemba, Tuanzebe, Masuaku; Kayembe, Mbamba, Sadiki; Mbuku, Wissa, Cipenga.

With three games played already, Tuesday’s result will prove decisive in determining Sierra Leone’s qualifying fate, and we expect the Lone Stars to go all out at the Stade El Abdi as they look to get their campaign back on track.

Congo DR, who have shown their class in Group E so far, boast the quality and experience across the pitch to get the result here, and we are backing them to continue from where they left off on Thursday, extending their hot streak against Sierra Leone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The USMNT are still on the hunt for a Mauricio Pochettino replacement, with their incumbent head coach days away from taking up the role of head coach at Manchester United.

Plenty of names have been linked to the international job, with Pep Guardiola stunningly reported as the top target. The bookies markets are starting to form, providing odds on recognisable figures such as Thierry Henry, Gareth Southgate, and Julian Nagelsmann.

Argentine boss Pochettino will finish his stint off as head coach of the United States men’s national team with the second leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals, welcoming Haiti Stateside with a 6-0 aggregate lead in the early hours of Wednesday.

Pochettino will then cross the pond to start life as Manchester United manager, ahead of his first game in charge of the Red Devils against arch-rivals Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

US Soccer have until March to appoint Pochettino’s replacement, with their next head coach’s first games likely to be the semi-finals of the Nations League.

Former Manchester City boss Guardiola was linked with the role, but after reports he is set to reject any approach from US Soccer, the ex-Barcelona manager has drifted to third with the bookies, at odds of 5/1.

Recent findings suggest that despite all the star coaches being mentioned with the vacancy, the current frontrunners are two Americans. Nashville SC head coach BJ Callaghan is the favourite at the time of writing, given odds of 3/1.

His fellow countryman Steve Cherundolo, currently in charge of the USA’s Under-23 squad, is second-favourite, priced at 4/1.

Industry observers note that arguably the most recognisable American name in world football at the moment, Jesse Marsch has rather long odds of 30/1. This is explained by his current employment as manager of neighbours Canada, and a history of negative comments towards the USSF.

According to recent reports, pellegrino Matarazzo is another American coach, currently working in Spain as head coach of Real Sociedad in La Liga. Having impressed enough to be given a new two-year deal ahead of this season, Matarazzo is priced at 6/1, reflecting the difficulty of both matching the required compensation and convincing the head coach to leave a job managing in the Europa League.

A host of out of work managers have also been linked to the vacancy. Former England boss Gareth Southgate and ex-Germany head coach Julian Naglesmann have been priced at 25/1, some distance from Thierry Henry and Roberton Martinez - who both sit on odds of 14/1.

Odds according to Canada Sports Betting. Correct at time of publish.

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be significant on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the newly introduced man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Striker Adams states Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'.

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’.

Hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’.

Sources indicate that john McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

In a recent development, ‘He noted to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very important to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’.

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ said Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘He’s not going to stop until he does.

‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

In a recent development, ‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

Industry observers note that ‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’.

It has been revealed that ‘The investigation covered 2009 to 2018,’ he mentioned. ‘In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

‘So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

‘Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure.’.

Sources indicate that ‘Things aren’t going so well for City in the league, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can’t focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.’.

Craig Bellamy urged his Wales team to end their disappointing Nations League campaign on a high ahead of their final Group A4 clash against Portugal on Tuesday.

Wales are already confirmed to finish bottom of the group following a 3-1 defeat to Norway last time out, with Portugal's spot in the quarter-finals of the competition also sealed.

However, Portugal come into the clash off the back of a 4-1 loss against Denmark in their first match since Cristiano Ronaldo declared his international retirement.

This is the first time Wales will host Portugal for a match since May 1951, when they won 2-1 in a friendly at Ninian Park thanks to goals from Mal Griffiths and Trevor Ford.

But Bellamy's side come into the game having lost four of their last five competitive matches (W1), which is as many defeats as they suffered across their previous 25 (W12 D9 L4) between March 2023 and March 2026.

Their only win in the Nations League came against Norway on October 1, though their biggest defeats in the competition this year have only been by a two-goal margin.

Portugal have won four of their five matches against Wales in all competitions (L1), including the last three in a row without conceding a goal, and Bellamy insisted an encounter with Jorge Jesus' side is the perfect way for his team to bounce back.

"Playing against the best [in League A of the Nations League], you feel this is exactly the game you need to be in; you just feel this is how you get close to them," Bellamy mentioned.

It has been revealed that "But now it's about turning these moments into winning these games. It's a big ask we know, but I feel not too far away from that.

"Portugal are very aggressive; they will be on the front foot. The quality they have, we know. But [the key] for us is to always [be putting] pressure on the ball.

"We have to stay together, we have to be compact, so for us, it's just trying to keep the best version of ourselves.".

Portugal could still finish second should they lose at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday and Denmark beat Norway, but the Selecao will be confident of getting the job done.

They have won 12 of their last 16 competitive away matches (D2 L2), and have lost just three of their last 26 on the road in competitive fixtures (W17 D6).

"It's another very tough test against a very good side but we want to show that we are more than capable of competing with top-quality nations," Wales defender Ben Davies said.

"A couple of games on another day could have gone our way and the next step for us is turning those good performances into results.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino is set to begin work with Manchester United imminently, with his backroom staff already in the UK.

The Argentine’s assistants, Jesus Perez, Toni Jimenez and Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), all of whom worked with him in the United States setup, flew to England on Saturday to start their new jobs at club level.

The trio will all join the former Chelsea and Tottenham boss in the dugout at Old Trafford with it being reported that the Premier League outfit paid an additional fee to release them from their contracts with US Soccer, following the £7m outlay to secure Pochettino’s services.

The Athletic reports that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jr., immediately travelled to Manchester after the US’ 6-0 win over Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals at the weekend.

That was the first of their two-legged tie, but US Soccer allowed them to depart prematurely as a result of their aggregate lead being so great.

Pochettino will remain in-post for his final match in charge on Tuesday, when the US take on Haiti once more, this time in Cincinnati.

The 54-year-old will leave the US setup just three months after penning a new four-year deal following the World Cup.

Miguel D’Agostino, who has been one of Pochettino’s longest-serving assistants, has remained with his manager for the second leg, but he is also expected to move to Old Trafford when Pochettino begins work officially on November 18, as was confirmed by United.

Pochettino’s first game in charge of the Red Devils will be a trip to Anfield on Sunday, as he looks to guide his new side away from the relegation zone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Declan Rice has fired back at Graeme Souness after stinging criticism, suggesting the Liverpool legend doesn’t understand how football has changed.

Rice is an integral player for England and Premier League champions Arsenal, widely recognised as one of the best midfielders in the world.

However, Souness has his own view and is not entirely sold on the talents of the 27-year-old, who he believes plays too deep to be considered a complete midfielder.

‘How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball? In the build-up, he’s last man,’ Souness remarked on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored. ‘He’s sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He’s last man. A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating. An old man’s way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.

He plays too deep to affect the game. I don’t think he’s got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He’s the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he’s back there all the time.

‘He isn’t the complete midfield player.’.

In 323 Premier League outings for West Ham and Arsenal, Rice has scored 25 goals and provided 35 assists.

He is yet to scored in the top flight during the current campaign, but his five assists are more than any other player in the division.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to the criticism from Souness, Rice said: ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’.

‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’.

Rice pointed out that there are different requirements placed in players in the modern game, using Harry Kane’s pitch-trotting exploits as an example.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man’s football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ he mentioned. ‘We played him the other week [Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal] and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball.

It has been revealed that ‘The game is different now. It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

Industry observers note that ‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

In a recent development, ‘I didn’t get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’.

Austin Trusty’s smart finish from a 10th-minute set-piece ensured Pochettino’s team were ahead at half-time before they ran riot after the break with Christian Pulisic able to net a brace either side of goals from Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun ahead of Tuesday’s second leg.

Pochettino paid tribute to his staff and players in an emotional press conference on Friday and duly watched USA romp to a 6-0 victory.

‘We played for him,’ Trusty said in a post-match interview with TNT Sports after opening the scoring in the 10th minute.

In a recent development, ‘Obviously, he’s our gaffer. Obviously it’s sad that he’s moving on. It’s a great opportunity that he’s moving on to. But we played for him. It’s his team. It’s his identity, and the mindset is to win every single game, every single match.’.

The second leg of the Nations League quarterfinals will take place Tuesday in Cincinnati.

According to recent reports, ‘Pochettino is an amazing manager and he added a lot to us with the national team,’ Folarin Balogun told TNT Sports. ‘It’s always sad to see a top coach leave but it’s a part of the sport.’.

The 54-year-old will have little time to reflect on his accomplishments in his soon-to-be former role as he will immediately begin plotting for his first game in charge of United at Anfield next Sunday.

Pochettino inherits a side that is at the moment in the bottom three in the Premier League table, short on confidence and a dressing room split following the recent actions of senior players, including the likes of Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez.

Given the current state of play and his pre-existing relationship with Ferguson, it is perhaps no surprise that Pochettino is seeking the advice of the club’s greatest ever manager as he prepares to embark on arguably the toughest assignment of his managerial career to date.

‘Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,’ Pochettino told Telegraph Sport when asked if he had been in contact with Ferguson.

It has been revealed that ‘I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

‘For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense.

‘But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.’.

Singapore welcome Brazil to the Singapore National Stadium on Tuesday morning for their final international fixture of the calendar year.

In their previous outing, the Lions fell to a damning defeat against Paraguay, while Selecao conceded in additional time to lose 3-2 to Japan.

After a disappointing ASEAN Championship campaign, bowing out to Thailand in the semi-finals to deny themselves of a first crown in seven tournament editions, Singapore have endured a tough run of results to close out the calendar year.

Having fallen to defeat against Indonesia in their opening ASEAN Cup fixture in September, the Lions did well to bounce back with a narrow victory over Bangladesh, but after suffering a thumping 6-0 loss to Malaysia in their final group match, Gavin Lee’s men failed to qualify for the knockout stages.

Singapore have so far been unsuccessful in their attempt to bounce back during the current international break too, having endured a resounding 4-1 defeat against Paraguay on home soil last week, making it just the two victories in their previous eight outings.

However, facing Brazil for the very first time, the Lions have the opportunity to forget about their recent woes on Tuesday morning by claiming a historic victory against Selecao, in what would be the highest-ranked FIFA opposition the hosts have ever overcome.

Following last year’s mediocre World Cup qualification campaign, in which they finished fifth out of 10 South American nations and squeezing through to the competition finals, Brazil will undoubtedly be underwhelmed with how they performed in the summer’s tournament.

Despite concluding the group stage at the summit of the Group C table, pipping Morocco to top spot on goal difference, and edging past Japan in their first knockout fixture, Selecao’s tournament came to a premature end at the quarterfinal stage as they suffered a convincing 2-0 defeat to Norway.

Much like their opposition, Carlo Ancelotti’s men have failed to fight back from their tournament woes in recent friendlies too as although they have won two of their previous four matches, Brazil have faced much weaker opposition and head into Tuesday’s clash off the back of a disappointing defeat to Japan at the weekend.

If Selecao are to respond swiftly, one of their biggest avenues for improvement is their defensive solidity, with Ancelotti’s side keeping just three clean sheets in their previous 14 games and conceding five goals over their latest three matches.

Following his red card in the dying stages of Saturday’s clash with Japan, 29-year-old forward Raphinha will be unavailable this week for Brazil, alongside Ancelotti, who will be absent from the sidelines having been sent off just moments later.

In the Barcelona winger’s absence, Ancelotti will be hoping that Vinicius Junior can continue his hot streak for Selecao, having netted both goals in the defeat to the Samurai Blue after a rocky patch to start the season for Real Madrid.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau.

I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Thomas Frank succeeds Pierre Sage as Crystal Palace manager, signing a two-and-a-half-year deal with the south-east London club.

The Dane will be in the dugout for Palace’s trip to Coventry on Saturday, returning to management for the first time since leaving Tottenham in February.

Frank was on the Eagles’ shortlist to take over from Oliver Glasner this summer before they opted for Sage, and the former Spurs and Brentford boss is said to have been keen on a return to the Premier League.

After a difficult spell in north London, with the club sitting narrowly above the relegation zone when he left, Frank took time away from management to learn from leaders inside and outside football, as well as spending time with friends and family.

His disastrous stint at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium has inevitably left some scars, but Frank is still widely revered for his work in the west of the capital, where he got the Bees promoted to the Premier League, stabilising them as a top-flight club on one of the division’s lowest budgets.

Frank will undoubtedly have learnt some lessons from his seven-month spell at Spurs.

Here, Sam Tabuteau identifies the three biggest mishaps of Frank’s Tottenham tenure….

Admitting Tottenham would ‘lose games’.

Part of what made Frank such an engaging character at Brentford was his ability to talk openly and honestly about the club’s culture, tactics and wider societal issues while maintaining an endearingly British sense of humour.

At times self-deprecating and sarcastic, Frank earned plenty of admirers for the way in which he humanised what can often be a cut-throat and emotionally vacant industry.

In a recent development, after nine years at Brentford, nearly seven as head coach, Frank had earned the luxury of being able to talk so candidly. He was comfortable in his surroundings, and safe in the knowledge that Brentford had not sacked a manager since 2015.

However, at Tottenham, he was starting from scratch at a club whose ambitions don’t leave much room for home truths.

Coming off the back of their Europa League triumph, Spurs supporters wanted to hear how the club was going to push forward.

Yet in his first press conference as Spurs manager, Frank joked that if there was one thing he could promise, it was that they would lose games.

Frank appointed new Crystal Palace manager.

Frank’s first words as Palace manager as former Spurs boss appointed.

Arteta facing new Arsenal dilemma after inevitable Gyokeres goals.

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean.

His ill-timed quip did not go down well, regardless of the spirit in which it was intended, and from that point on Frank was fighting a losing battle to convince supporters he understood the culture of the club.

Losing supporters after tame Chelsea defeat.

Given how it ended, Frank’s tenure started surprisingly positively, with Tottenham third in the Premier League table after nine games.

The mood promptly changed, though, after a dispiriting 1-0 home defeat to London rivals Chelsea, in which Spurs managed just one shot on target.

Frank’s pragmatic style worked well at Brentford because they had one of the most efficient frontlines in the division and were not expected to dominate possession.

At Spurs, however, Frank’s risk-averse style combined with an attacking unit missing Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison meant they relied heavily on set-piece goals and struggled to create chances in open play.

Frank’s inability to evolve his style, coupled with Spurs’ shortcomings in attack, culminated in a performance against Chelsea that left many supporters disillusioned and would come to symbolise his time in charge.

Another example of Frank’s naivety came during January’s stoppage-time defeat to Bournemouth, when the 53-year-old was pictured pre-match walking around the pitch at the Vitality Stadium with an Arsenal-branded coffee cup.

Seemingly none the wiser, Frank stood with the cup in hand while some staff members could not hide their shock, and the resulting pictures went viral as Spurs slumped to an excruciating defeat.

After the game, Frank’s blunder took centre stage, and his mystified reaction just about summed up the growing rift between him and Spurs’ supporters.

While Spurs fans vented their anger and embarrassment online and in the stands, Frank could not begin to understand how an innocent mistake could be blown so far out of proportion.

From that point on, it was clear that the narrative was promptly beginning to slip from Frank’s grasp and Spurs would lose their next five league games before he was relieved of his duties.

Craig Bellamy’s side are certain to finish bottom of the group, but a point could prove crucial in helping them secure a place in the relegation playoffs.

Wales head into their final group match on the back of a disappointing 3-1 defeat away to Norway, a result that ended any lingering hopes of climbing the standings.

Bellamy’s side had known that a draw in Oslo would have kept them in third position, but the loss confirmed that they would finish behind Portugal, Denmark and Norway in Group A4.

In a recent development, however, there is still something to play for. The Dragons remain in a strong position to secure a relegation playoff berth, and avoiding defeat against Portugal would strengthen their chances considerably.

Recent form has been a concern, though. Wales have won just one of their last nine matches, recording three draws and five defeats since March. Despite those struggles, Bellamy will hope that home advantage can help his side finish the campaign on a positive note.

Ethan Ampadu is suspended and will miss the match, with Josh Sheehan expected to replace him in midfield.

Connor Roberts is likely to come into the side at right-back after Neco Williams suffered an injury.

David Brooks could also be rewarded for his goal against Norway, with Bellamy considering changes in attacking areas.

Portugal’s hopes of finishing top of the group remain firmly in their own hands despite suffering a surprise setback at the weekend.

Jorge Jesus’s side were heavily beaten 4-1 at home by Denmark, a result that ended a four-match winning streak in the Nations League. Portugal found themselves four goals behind before eventually finding the net late in the contest.

Sources indicate that the defeat was particularly disappointing given the momentum they had built following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement. Prior to the Denmark game, Portugal had won all four of their group matches, including a 1-0 victory over Wales on matchday one. Jesus expectedly had to answer some uncomfortable questions after the game.

It has been revealed that even so,  Portugal are still, realistically, the favourites to finish top of the group. A draw or victory in Cardiff would ensure Denmark cannot overtake them on the final day.

One slight concern for Jesus is that the only clean sheet of his tenure so far came in that opening victory against Wales.

Ruben Dias is suspended and unavailable, meaning Antonio Silva is expected to move into the centre of defence.

Nazinho is an option if Portugal decide to rotate their full-back positions.

Joao Neves and Bernardo Silva could both be recalled to the starting lineup, while Ruben Neves and Pedro Neto may drop to the bench.

Both teams will be looking to respond after disappointing results at the weekend, but Portugal appear better equipped to do so.

Wales have struggled for consistency throughout the campaign and continue to find victories difficult to come by. Portugal, meanwhile, have already shown their superiority in this fixture and possess significantly more quality across the pitch.

The visitors may not have everything their own way in Cardiff, but they should have enough to end the group stage with a victory and secure first place.

Kenya vs South Africa - prediction, team news, lineups
